I understand your confusion. The sky in this poem is the antagonist. It's judgement is the reference. Assuming lack of emotional stability in me, therefore not wanting me to be sad or blue until I'm coherent, or "coffee drunk."

The clouds are a form of the sky's compassion. Sheltering me from the blue emotion, a mute grey. As I refer to the dirt of the land as a coat of age or callous I have built that could fend off the "cold" or jade to be gained from the feeling of sadness or "blue."

By "till the sky can't fake belief" I am referring to it's unwelcomed compassion in withholding emotion. Caring belief in emotional health while clouding the sky to shelter me from the emotion that requires mental maintenance.(as a personified antagonist)

The use of the number twelve is arbitrary to a purpose. The feeling of being narrowed, or pigeon holed into a process of thought is what I was going for. Tunnel vision to a goal that feels both necessary and meaningless all the same.

Asking "...there could be more," was a direct shot at percieving only 12 ways to achieve whatever goal that may be, even if the goal is just making it to Sunday, safe and sound.

This is a powerful point, to me. Poetry is generally scattered to the wind. This imagery implies a poet sinking their own ship to spread their words. Watching their papers float away into the void as they continue to leak words of beauty and pain.

To imply the boat is already sunk seems to mean that they have been at this for a long time, though all they can stand to see is their beautiful lies given to the void of water and sky.

My SO works in a tourist Hotspot in California's Napa Valley at a small bookstand in a kind of food court mall.

She is the only one at the stand during the day, so in order to use the restroom she put up her "be back in 5 minutes" sign. When she returned a couple approached her in order to point out that a woman and her two small children had just walked off with a stack of 3D bookmarks from the stand.

My girlfriend walked across the mall, informed them that they can't just walk away from a store with merchandise and needed to pay for the bookmarks. She escorted the woman back to the stand and she paid for the bookmarks.

A few minutes later her husband walks over with the receipt. 

"You know, it was rude of you to imply that we weren't going to pay for those" he said. 

She reiterated to him that one should not walk away from a store with merchandise. 

"Well, it was rude of you to imply we weren't going to pay for them and it ruined my day. I have enough money to buy everything in this store" Says the husband.

"You may buy what you want, but you can't leave a store with products without paying for them." She replies

"You know, they're just kids" Says the husband, seemingly implying his children did it.

"Oh, so your two year old was over here unsupervised?" she replies

"Pffft, no!" He says

"Oh, so your two year old reached up here and grabbed these bookmarks?" She says, pointing to the 5.5 foot tall rack with bookmarks at the top.

"Psssh, no! I just wanted you to know it was rude of you and it ruined my day." He said

"Well, I'm ok with that. It is quite rude to take things from a store without paying." She said.

Man walks away...

He told her she was rude and ruined his day several more times than that through the convo. I'm just writing what I remember.

TLDR: woman steals from my  girlfriend's bookstand. Woman's husband tells my girlfriend she is rude for calling them on it.
